take_homes: A licence rollout is not adoption. Seats activated and seats used are two different numbers, and we report the wrong one.
Before buying or building anything, ask the actual person how they do the job today. That is what the new thing has to beat.
A plan with unnamed owners is not a plan. Someone has to answer for it, and that doesn't come with the tool.

monday.move: Ask my controller how the month-end variance commentary gets done today: who writes it, how long it takes, who reads it. Don't try an agent yet.
monday.stop_condition: If it takes under an hour or nobody reads it, drop it. No saving to check.
monday.blocker: IT has not approved the tool for finance data, so even a good result can't be tried properly.

misconception.why: I still think of AI as a licence with a price per seat. But the point that access and use get reported as one number matches our failed rollouts, where the licences were bought and nothing changed. I'm not yet convinced the organisation has to build the capability, because nothing in the module gave me a cost or a payback.

one_line: Good point that handing out access isn't the same as people using it, and the pre-mortem question is useful. But it never gave me a cost, a payback or a number, and it assumes you've already built an agent.
